extra_misconceptions.fact: High-voltage capacitors retain lethal electrical charges long after unplugging and must never be touched during an inspection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unplugging a television or microwave from the wall outlet immediately removes all electrical shock hazards inside the casing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Appliance creation requires materials engineers for heat plastics, electrical engineers for circuits, and manufacturing teams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mechanical engineers alone design household appliances without input from electrical, materials, or manufacturing engineers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineers often specify nylon sacrificial gears to shear safely under a jam and protect the expensive electric motor from burning out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plastic gears inside a cordless drill or kitchen mixer are chosen only to lower production cost rather than for engineering reasons.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Puncturing a lithium-ion cell triggers thermal runaway and fire, so battery subsystems must be studied only from external labels.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Investigating how a sealed lithium-ion battery pack works requires prying open the metal cell pouch with a flathead screwdriver.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to pry open a household appliance before unplugging the power cord and discharging internal capacitors?
What happens to your reassembly accuracy when you photograph each fastener layer and wire connection before removing parts?
Which physical indicator inside a toaster distinguishes a thermal bimetallic switch from a resistive nichrome heating element?
What measurement confirms whether a motor gear train inside a toy increases rotational torque or increases output shaft speed?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Landmark projects succeed through iterative testing, prototype failures, and continuous redesigns when field obstacles appear.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Major engineering achievements like the Golden Gate Bridge or Apollo 11 succeeded because the initial blueprints had zero flaws.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scientists discover natural laws, whereas engineers apply those laws within cost, material, and safety limits to build solutions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scientific discovery and engineering achievement are identical activities that follow the exact same research goals and methods.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Megaprojects rely on hundreds of specialized engineers coordinating across geotechnical, metallurgical, and systems disciplines.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: One famous chief engineer single-handedly solves every structural, electrical, and logistical obstacle on a historic megaproject.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every major feat introduces trade-offs, such as dam sediment buildup or grid load demands, that require ongoing engineering care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Engineering achievements only benefit society and never create secondary environmental or infrastructure challenges to manage.

extra_socratic_questions: What primary source records reveal how the chief engineers on your chosen project solved unexpected soil, thermal, or load failures?
Under what condition does a pure scientific discovery become a practical engineering achievement that serves millions of people?
What quantitative metric best documents how the Panama Canal or Apollo program changed global transport speed or reliability?
Which safety standards emerged only after engineers analyzed structural failures or worker hazards on landmark construction projects?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Architects focus on spatial form and building use, while civil engineers calculate structural loads, foundations, and fluid flow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Civil engineers and architects perform the exact same job when designing skyscrapers, bridges, and municipal water systems.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Chemical engineers scale lab reactions into full industrial plants by managing heat transfer, fluid piping, and reactor safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Chemical engineers spend their careers mixing small test tubes in a laboratory exactly like research chemists do every day.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Embedded systems require electrical and mechanical engineers to co-design circuit boards that survive heat, shock, and enclosure size.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Software and electrical engineers work in isolated silos and never need to understand mechanical vibration or thermal limits.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industrial engineers analyze cycle times, ergonomics, and statistical process control to reduce waste across entire organizations.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Industrial engineers only repair factory conveyor belts rather than optimizing human workflows, supply chains, and quality systems.

extra_socratic_questions: Where does the responsibility of a chemical engineer end and the work of a mechanical engineer begin inside a battery factory?
What shared mathematical and physical principles connect civil structural analysis with aerospace airframe stress calculations?
Which test measurements must an electrical engineer and a biomedical engineer exchange when building a wearable heart monitor?
Why is it dangerous to design a highway bridge using only civil traffic load models without geotechnical soil bearing data?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern engineers spend much of their time collaborating in teams, writing specifications, reviewing CAD models, and testing data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional engineers spend ninety percent of their workday alone at a desk solving calculus equations by hand on paper.

extra_misconceptions.fact: CAD tools only geometry-model what the user inputs; engineers must still verify material limits, tolerances, and physical test loads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Computer-aided design software automatically guarantees that a 3D model can be manufactured safely and will not fail under load.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineering results must be clearly documented in reports, peer-reviewed for errors, and presented to fabrication and client teams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An engineer's job ends the moment a technical drawing or calculation spreadsheet is finished on their workstation computer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Manufacturing floors and test labs mandate closed-toe shoes, eye protection, and host escort briefings before visitors enter.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visiting an engineering workplace only requires casual clothing and a notebook without checking facility safety rules beforehand.

extra_socratic_questions: What question during your interview uncovers how the engineer validates computer simulation outputs against physical test results?
Which project constraint forced your interviewed engineer to trade peak theoretical performance for lower cost or manufacturability?
What peer review checklists and revision logs does the engineer use to communicate test results to clients and team members?
Where should a Scout verify personal protective equipment and site visitor rules before touring an active engineering lab or plant?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Systems engineering starts by defining user needs and measurable constraints, then compares alternatives before building a prototype.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Systems engineering means building the first idea that comes to mind and writing down the specifications after it is finished.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prototype test failures provide essential feedback data that guides the next design iteration to strengthen weak interfaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A prototype test that bends, jams, or falls short of the target metric proves that the systems engineering process has failed.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Overbuilding individual parts can make a camp system too heavy to carry; systems engineering balances interfaces across the whole unit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Optimizing every single component for maximum strength and weight always produces the best overall patrol equipment system.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A buildable engineering design requires dimensioned drawings, tolerances, and a material list so another person can reproduce it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sketching a rough picture without dimensions, material callouts, or bill of materials is sufficient for an engineering design plan.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your patrol gear build if you jump straight to cutting materials before writing measurable design requirements?
Which criterion in a systems engineering trade matrix separates a mandatory safety constraint from a nice-to-have design wish?
What measurement confirms that your prototype device actually meets your original weight, load, or setup-time target in camp?
Why is it dangerous to test a load-bearing garage or patrol device to failure without setting up a clear drop zone and eye gear?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Simple machines cannot create energy; multiplying force by four requires pulling the input rope or lever four times the distance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A lever or pulley system that multiplies lifting force by four also multiplies the total mechanical energy output by four.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Friction at pivot pins, gear teeth, and sliding surfaces always reduces actual mechanical advantage below the ideal geometric ratio.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ideal mechanical advantage and actual measured mechanical advantage are identical in real wood, plastic, and metal mechanisms.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A wedge is two inclined planes placed back-to-back, and a screw is an inclined plane wrapped helically around a central cylinder.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Screws and wedges are completely unrelated to inclined planes and operate on entirely different physical principles of force.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gearing up for higher rotational speed proportionally reduces output torque, while gearing down increases torque at lower speed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Increasing the gear ratio to spin an output wheel faster also increases the twisting torque available to climb a steep ramp.

extra_socratic_questions: What mechanical trade-off occurs between input force and travel distance when you move a lever fulcrum closer to the heavy load?
Which linkage or cam geometry converts continuous rotary shaft motion into back-and-forth linear reciprocating motion in your model?
What measurement confirms the actual mechanical advantage of your inclined plane or pulley model compared to its ideal ratio?
Where should a Scout position hands and clamps when cutting dowels, tensioning springs, or testing moving gears on a workbench?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A college graduate must pass the FE exam, work four years under a PE, and pass the PE exam before earning state licensure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating from an accredited four-year university engineering program automatically grants the legal title of Professional Engineer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stamping a plan means the PE took responsible charge of the design and accepts personal legal liability for public safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Professional Engineer stamp is merely a rubber-stamp formality that transfers all legal liability to the construction contractor.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Licensing boards require Professional Engineers to seal only drawings within their tested area of technical competence.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A licensed civil Professional Engineer is legally permitted to stamp complex electrical grid or chemical plant designs outside their field.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most state boards require licensed Professional Engineers to log continuing professional development hours to maintain registration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Once an engineer passes the PE exam, their license stays active forever without any continuing education or ethics renewal.

extra_socratic_questions: What four milestones in education, examination, and supervised experience must an engineer complete to earn a state PE license?
Under what legal condition must engineering blueprints be stamped by a licensed Professional Engineer rather than an unlicensed grad?
What verification records must a Professional Engineer review and retain before placing a signed seal on public bridge drawings?
Why is it dangerous to allow unsealed structural or municipal water designs to go into public construction without PE oversight?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The first fundamental canon of engineering ethics requires engineers to hold paramount the safety, health, and welfare of the public.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An engineer's highest ethical duty under the Code of Ethics is to maximize employer profits and keep every client request secret.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Falsifying or selectively omitting test data violates engineering ethics and can cause catastrophic structural or mechanical failure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rounding down an unfavorable stress test measurement to pass an inspection is acceptable if the project is behind schedule.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Undisclosed vendor gifts create a conflict of interest that compromises objective engineering judgment and violates ethical canons.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Accepting undisclosed gifts from a material vendor is harmless as long as the vendor's steel meets the minimum specification.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Both codes demand honesty, public service, environmental stewardship, and the courage to speak truth when safety is at risk.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Scout Oath and Law apply only to youth camping activities and have little in common with professional engineering rules.

extra_socratic_questions: What must an engineer do first when a manager pressures them to approve a part that failed its safety factor test in the lab?
Which canon of the Engineer's Code of Ethics directly parallels the Scout Law mandate to remain trustworthy and brave under pressure?
Why is it dangerous to alter or omit a single outlier data point from an official engineering test log to meet a launch deadline?
Where should a practicing engineer report an unresolved public safety hazard when internal project leadership refuses to halt work?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineers must pass the FE exam, log four years of supervised work, and pass the PE exam before stamping public plans.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating with a four-year bachelor's degree in engineering automatically grants legal authority to stamp public drawings.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most state licensing boards require a degree from an ABET-accredited program to qualify for standard FE and PE licensure tracks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any university engineering program qualifies a graduate to sit for state Fundamentals of Engineering licensure exams.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Practicing engineers spend significant time in cross-functional teams writing specs, testing prototypes, and reviewing budgets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Entry-level engineers spend their entire workday alone at a computer running CAD models and mathematical calculations.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Complete education cost estimates must include lab fees, software, living expenses, exam fees, and paid co-op salary offsets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Total college tuition is the only financial cost to evaluate when researching an engineering education pathway.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must you obtain parent or guardian permission and follow two-deep leadership before interviewing a practicing engineer?
What legal authority distinguishes a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) from a graduate who only passed the FE exam?
Which Bureau of Labor Statistics metric reveals whether an engineering specialty is growing faster than the national average?
Under what condition does an ABET-accredited engineering degree shorten the experience required for state PE licensure?
